headlines.title: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, way more than expected; unemployment rate slips to 4.1%
headlines.summary: A blowout payrolls print — 165K vs. 59K expected — is the kind of number that reprices everything from the long bond to the front end of the curve in about 90 seconds. With Pimco already calling multiple Fed hikes 'reasonable' and gold dropping on the print, this is the tape-mover that makes Thursday's AI selloff look like a sideshow. Every rate-sensitive sector — tech, real estate, utilities — has to recalibrate right now.

headlines.title: Markets plunge as Wall Street heads for its worst post-midterm day since 1896
headlines.summary: The Dow down 1,200, the S&P off 3.3%, the Nasdaq flirting with correction territory — this is the kind of session that rewrites positioning across every desk on the Street. The Democratic sweep spooked the AI trade hard, with $2 trillion wiped from the Nasdaq 100 alone, dragging chips, data center plays, and crypto down with it. When retail is dumping at Covid-selloff pace and options volumes hit all-time records, you don't need a PhD to know the bid has left the building.

headlines.title: The AI 'credit card' is getting costlier as CoreWeave bond yield tops 16%
headlines.summary: When the junk paper funding the AI buildout starts yielding 16%, the whole capital structure of the trade is in question — and ING reportedly trying to offload $500 million in data center loans is the canary in that coal mine. This isn't just a CoreWeave story; it's a signal that the credit markets are starting to price in what equity investors are only beginning to fear. If the debt spigot tightens, the hyperscalers' capex plans don't survive contact with a Democratic Congress and a hawkish Fed.
